editorText:
The Ignotius’s coffee machine mysterious as it was with it's seamless aesthetic integrated into the mess of the alien like ship drawing little attention to it’s users. While the novelty of a mess was completely redundant to the sentient's Doc had taken it upon himself with a foresight to design the Sentient mother-ship as a benchmark for encouraging an inter human - sentient relationship, Despite it’s current short-comings.

“Your coffee John!" the voice of the Ignatius AI system spoke with a sense of camaraderie. While it wasn't as cheerful and cute as kitten, it imbued it's guests with a sense of metallic integrity. John pressed the to his lips to the edge of his coffee cup taking his first sip. Steam danced with his nostrils warming his soul as he drank. "smells like home” he thought, then began to ponder what the universe had in store for him with respect to any sort of home moving forward.

"Good morning Cap" Shai made her way through the mess doors with a joyous stride in her step, born renewed from a good night’s sleep, her positive and cheerful self again.."I'll take a spiced Chai thanks Ignotius”. John raised his eyebrows wondering if her request was a question or a request himself, then raised his cup for another sip. “I’ve been meaning to talk to you all about something” said John, his tone soft and almost shy, not his normal confident self. It was almost like a sense of guilt shadowed his tone.

"What’s got you bothered Cap?"Shai smiled as she raised the fresh steaming Chai she had just grabbed from the coffee vending machine, as she inhaled, the aromatic spices cleared her sinuses. She smiled at John taking her first sip of Chai. John met her smile with an obliged smile, then sat quietly just appreciating how approachable she was as a person.

Tau entered the room, Tex following behind her barely fitting through the door frame to the mess. She looked at John with a subtle smile, tilting her head with camaraderie."Captain" her voice seemed less cheerful, but more professional this time as though their situation despite the quiet after what felt like a never ending storm, was still dire, and she was ready for anything at a moments notice.

Tex was still his usual self throwing a half cocked cheerful smile across the room attending to his meal with utmost importance. After all the big guy needed to eat. Except the eagerness to overpower the metallic taste left in his mouth from the nutrients fed to them in oversleep was obvious. They all felt his eagerness and respected his silence.

“You know you can eat that in more than three bites right Tex” Shai chuckled to herself. John his mood lightened by Shai’s banter let out a little smile, then drew the rooms attention this time coming back with more authority in his tone now that the others were present, yet it was strange as though he was disengaged. Like he was releasing an injured animal he had nurtured back to good health back to the wild, shooing it away. “You no longer need to call me captain.. “I am not your captain anymore”. John paused for a moment to think.

The room fell silent, Tex even stopped stuffing his face for a moment, waiting momentarily for John to keep talking, but resumed a second later slowly raising his fork loaded with curry back to his mouth, his eyes still fixed on John.

Still sipping her chai, Shai looked over to Take, then Tex, Reading the room to see if she had missed anything. "Wait a minute… what are you trying to say John?"

Tex joined in “Yeah big guy, you aren’t getting cold feet on us are you” He said with a hint of sarcasm, he pushed out his chair looking directly at John’s metallic shins. He thought himself clever for a moment.

John took in a deep breath. “Look… None of you would be in this situation if  hadn’t stepped into that dam pod”. John expressed his message with an intensity in his eyes, his palms open on the table, his coffee sat half full getting colder.

Tex started eating again. “What I’m trying to say is I am no longer your captain, you aren’t bound to me under any protectant law.. There is no council to call on you here, No Court Marshal, you are all free to make lives for yourselves as you please on oasis”. John paused for a moment, it was as though he couldn’t really believe what he was about to propose himself, “or return if you like”. Tau leant into the centre of the table concern stricken brows and deep brown eyes veering into John’s soul. “Return?” said Tau. “Yes” said John, “I have already spoken to Doc and he is happy to arrange safe passage and negotiation terms to have you all reinstated, although”. Tex laughed almost choking on the gristly curried beef chunk he’d been chewing on now these past minutes.

“Fuck that guy, the only instating I’ll be doing is instating my as a permanent  fixture in his ass”. Tex paused cooling off for a moment as the room fell silent in agreeance with him then started back up again as his face turned once again to frustration. “I mean.. Where the fuck have you been? Did you not see the barrage of missiles & rail slugs he hurled at us? He wants us dead, to cover up his own fucking mess”, Tau was still, emotionless sitting up straight staring into space in the middle of the table, but she seemed calculated despite Tex’s apparent frustration “He wants control, Tex is right, we took that from him” said Tau “It isn’t a matter of cleaning up a mess” Said John

 “The worker bot project was a complete success in the eyes of the Engineer that created them, Just not Marcellus” John couldn’t allow minor details to poison the view of what he had grown to trust and now become a part of. He had seen the world from behind the Sentient eyes, seen them lay themselves down when they could have so easily taken over, He had seen how effective they had become in leading through virtue and not destruction.

“We are part of something much bigger than ourselves now” John continued. “Marcellus wants control, and if anyone has seen what really went on down there, which I have, He can’t have that information getting out and appealing to the ethics of others.”  John concluded. “So no Tex, I didn’t miss the barrage of rail gun fire pointed right at us. I’m the one that’s compromised, I’m the one Marcellus wants”

Tau intervened “We’ve all seen what went on down there, we’ve all seen too much, it doesn’t matter what we are at this stage it’s what we know, There’s no way Marcellus will just let that fly … ”

Tau veered toward John her face was pure disbelief, she didn’t believe for a moment what John was saying was possible. “According to Doc, a full memory wipe of the events as they occurred is possible and scans can show, It will be like it never happened” John was convincing in his soft yet concise tone. But the room stirred still Tex sat disgruntled in the corner devouring his meal in what seemed like a contained focus, different to what Tex would normally do forking an assault on the steaming curry lab grown beef that somehow put up a fight with a genetically grown layers of fat.

Tex still wasn’t convinced “Who the hell even is this guy Doc and why do you trust him so much”. John paused, taking in a deep breath to prepare himself for what he was about to tell his closest friends, in reality the only organic family he had left. He prepared He preparing himself for the insanity of it all, imagining how he came to accept it, in all his optimism and how in Sol these few before him with all their known imperfections would take being told that his own biological father is a live walking breathing talking amalgamation of technology.

“They won’t believe me, you’ve been dead almost 50 years” John thought to himself. Although he wasn’t the only one listening. “They don’t need to believe it, they only need to see it with their own eyes”. In that moment John felt chills moving down his spine. “Get out of my hea…” He thought, but what he was thinking wasn’t just thought it was very real.
